A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same advertisement-creativity study. Their main text, tables, figures, equations, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original human annotations and VLM evaluations on Creative-100 and Atypical-300, including distribution modeling, disagreement prediction, and pairwise preference results in Table 2.

after.justification: v2 retains these original annotation and evaluation results and adds descriptive score summaries in Section 5 and Appendix A.1.

M1.justification: The same zero-shot prompting procedures for distribution modeling, disagreement prediction, and pairwise preference remain. The model checkpoints and prompts in Appendix C are unchanged; expanded explanations do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Creative-100 and Atypical-300 datasets and tasks. Section 3.1 corrects the topic list to match the ten sampled groups already stated in v1 Appendix A.3; this does not establish changed dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains LLaVA-7B, LLaVA-13B, InternVL2-8B, and GPT-4v in the same comparisons. GPT-4v distribution modeling remains omitted for budget reasons. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The metrics, pair-selection threshold of 0.5, pair counts, median-based easy/hard division, annotation processing, and generation temperatures are unchanged. v2 clarifies existing procedures without reporting revised settings or a new evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Section 5 adds a descriptive comparison of model and human score levels to investigate differing metric rankings. Appendix A.1 adds a scored example illustrating originality without strong atypicality. Existing easy/hard comparisons, error analyses, and word clouds are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same three distribution-modeling runs in Appendix C.3 and Table 3, alongside the same correlation p-values and significance convention. No new repetitions, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical tests are reported.

E6.justification: Existing table results and Figure 1 values are unchanged. v2 newly reports average scores of 2.19 for LLaVA-13B, 2.31 for InternVL2-8B, and 1.94 for humans in Section 5. Appendix A.1 also reports atypicality 1.56 and originality 2.0 for the new Figure 2 example.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 retains the same distribution-sampling inequality, constants, and argument for 25 annotations. The new intrinsic/extrinsic explanation of creativity dimensions is conceptual rather than a new mathematical definition, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The benchmark and three-task contributions remain. However, v2's conclusion includes distribution modeling among tasks VLMs still struggle with, whereas v1 describes alignment in distribution modeling and singles out disagreement prediction as challenging. This modestly weakens the concluding assessment despite positive language retained elsewhere.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of the KL-versus-correlation ranking difference and hypotheses linking disagreement failures to background knowledge and multi-step reasoning. It also explains the dimensions' complementarity and newly connects the absence of fine-tuning to dataset size. These refine discussion of unchanged experiments; demographic-bias discussion largely moves to Ethical Consideration.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies vllm 0.6.1.post1 and identifies the H2P computing resource. The advertised repository path changes from ads_creativity to ads-creativity, although the PDFs do not establish changed availability. Existing checkpoints, GPU specifications, prompts, and runtimes remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction and Section 2 substantially expand creativity-specific positioning across psychology, machine creativity, writing, mathematical/code problem solving, psychological tests, and question answering. The generic automatic-evaluation discussion is replaced, and v2 explicitly distinguishes its advertisement-understanding focus from Zhong et al. (2024) on multimodal humor generation.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the opening motivation and related work, reorganizes the dataset explanation, and expands the results narrative and conclusion. Broad wording edits accompany a separate Ethical Consideration section and a new acknowledgment, constituting substantial editorial revision.

P2.justification: v2 reformats Figure 1 and revises its caption, adds illustrative Figures 2 and 3, and rearranges existing demographic and sampling-bound figures around the appendix text. Existing result tables retain their structures, and the remaining appendix images are preserved with updated numbering.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity and research context through the rewritten related work, clearer distinction between creativity dimensions, limited score analysis, and added implementation information. The empirical foundation remains unchanged. Its more negative conclusion about distribution modeling is less consistent with the retained positive results discussion, but the explanatory gains support a modest net improvement.
